source_name: Gjirafa.biz — Kosovo business directory (Western Union / money transfer agent listings)
why_relevant: Local business directory that enumerates MTO agent locations and financial-service outlets across Kosovo — a workable proxy for mapping the physical remittance distribution network, which no operator publishes in structured form.

source_name: PPRC/KRPP Open Contracting (OCDS) bulk data & API — OCP Data Registry entry
source_subtype: structured open data mirror / API registry
why_relevant: The Kosovo Public Procurement Regulatory Commission publishes the full e-Prokurimi contracting cycle as Open Contracting Data Standard (OCDS) via API since 2021; the OCP registry mirrors it for download in JSON/Excel/CSV by year or all-time. This is the machine-readable backbone for systematically extracting every banking/payment-services award: buyer, supplier, lots, values, procedure type, dates.

source_name: KRPP / Public Procurement Regulatory Commission (PPRC) institutional site — rules, forms, annual procurement reports
source_subtype: regulator legal framework / standard forms / annual reports
why_relevant: The regulator's rules and standard forms define the notice taxonomy (B05 njoftim per kontrate, B08 njoftim per dhenie te kontrates, B58 etc.), thresholds, and the multilingual publication obligation for contracts >=EUR 500,000 (sq/sr/en). Essential for building reliable parsers and for knowing which notice types carry award value and scope. KRPP annual reports aggregate spend by category and authority.

source_name: Prokurimi i Hapur — Open & Transparent Procurement Portal (Lëvizja FOL / Demokraci Plus, USAID TEAM)
why_relevant: Civil-society portal that ingests e-Prokurimi data via the OCDS API and presents contracts, contracting authorities and economic operators in a searchable, analyst-friendly way. Far easier to query for supplier-side views (e.g. all contracts won by a given bank or payment vendor) than the government portal, and it carries history from 2020 onward.

source_name: Flamujt e Kuq / Red Flags — corruption-risk monitor on Kosovo contracts (Demokraci Plus)
source_subtype: CSO analytics tool over procurement API
why_relevant: Automatically pulls signed public contracts from e-Prokurimi via the OCDS API from 1 Jan 2020 onward and scores them against red-flag indicators (single bidder, negotiated procedure without notice, value deviation). Useful both as an alternative structured index of awards and as a filter for anomalous banking/payment tenders worth deeper reading.

source_name: OSHP — Organi Shqyrtues i Prokurimit (Procurement Review Body) decisions
why_relevant: OSHP adjudicates bidder complaints; its decisions reveal who bid, on what technical specification, at what price, and why an award was annulled or upheld — including for banking, card and payment-system tenders. Complaint files often disclose competitive detail (pricing, technical disqualification grounds) never present in the award notice itself.

source_name: Databaza e vendimeve të OSHP (Demokraci Plus mirror)
why_relevant: NGO-built searchable mirror/database of Procurement Review Body decisions, typically more scrapable and better indexed than the official site; useful redundancy if the official OSHP search is JS-heavy or unstable.

source_name: AQP — Agjencia Qendrore e Prokurimit (Central Procurement Agency) centralised contracts
why_relevant: AQP runs centralised and framework contracts on behalf of the whole central and local government. If banking, card, POS acceptance or payment-processing services are ever bought once for many authorities, the contract sits here — a single high-value award with pan-government scope. AQP also publishes signed contract PDFs and periodic reports.

source_name: BQK — Central Bank of Kosovo procurement / tenders page (Tenderët, Shpalljet)
why_relevant: The central bank is itself a contracting authority and a buyer of payment-system infrastructure (RTGS/ACH, instant payments, card switch, security, core systems) as well as ordinary services. Its own tender and award notices reveal national payment-infrastructure modernisation before any vendor announcement. It publishes notices in Albanian, Serbian and English and has its own procurement rules.

source_name: Kosovo Customs (Dogana e Kosovës) procurement announcement folder — worked example of authority-level B08 publication
why_relevant: Demonstrates the widespread pattern that individual contracting authorities also mirror their B05/B08 notices as PDFs in predictable shared folders on their own domains. Customs and the Tax Administration are directly relevant buyers of payment collection, POS acceptance and card-based revenue services. These authority-level mirrors are often easier to crawl than the central portal and catch notices the portal search hides.

source_name: ATK / Tax Administration of Kosovo (PAK/ATK) procurement notices — Serbian-language notice example
why_relevant: The tax administration publishes 'OBAVEŠTENJE O DODELI UGOVORA' (contract award notice) in Serbian, confirming the sr-language notice channel exists on authority sites. ATK is a relevant buyer of payment-collection, e-filing and card/POS acceptance services, and its Serbian notices provide the sr vocabulary needed for full-language coverage.

source_name: NJPMNP — Unit for Public Enterprise Policy and Monitoring, Ministry of Economy (list of central & local POEs)
why_relevant: Authoritative actor map of Kosovo's publicly owned enterprises (central POEs such as KEK, KOSTT, Posta, water/waste utilities, plus ~55 local POEs). Utilities are the largest institutional buyers of bill-payment acceptance, POS/kiosk collection, payroll and cash-management banking services. Needed to enumerate the contracting authorities whose e-Prokurimi records must be tracked.

source_name: Prishtina Online — procurement directory of central institutions and municipalities
why_relevant: Aggregator listing central institutions and their procurement pages/contacts. Useful as a shortcut actor map for enumerating contracting authorities and their local procurement sections, especially where an authority does not mirror notices to the central portal cleanly.

source_name: BidsFactory — Kosovo e-Prokurimi tender aggregator
why_relevant: Commercial aggregator republishing Kosovo e-Prokurimi notices with English translation and CPV filtering. Useful for cross-language discovery and as an alerting layer, and helps confirm whether a notice existed if the official portal record becomes hard to retrieve.

source_name: World Bank corporate & project procurement notices for Kosovo (incl. 'Electronic Payment Acceptance in Kosovo')
source_subtype: IFI/donor procurement notice & contract award database
why_relevant: Donor-funded procurement is a parallel public-sector buying route that bypasses e-Prokurimi. The World Bank, working with the Central Bank of Kosovo, solicited an assessment of Kosovo's electronic payments acceptance landscape; the Strengthening Digital Governance for Service Delivery project (P178162) procures shared digital platforms. These notices and awards reveal payment-market interventions, budgets and winning consultancies/vendors.

source_name: UNDP Procurement Notices portal (country filter Kosovo)
why_relevant: UNDP procures IT, payments and financial-inclusion consultancy on behalf of Kosovo public bodies; notices and awards give scope and budget for donor-funded payment/digital-finance work outside the national portal.

source_name: DevelopmentAid — donor tender & award tracker for Kosovo ICT/finance projects
why_relevant: Aggregates IFI/EU/bilateral tenders and awards for Kosovo, including the World Bank digital governance platform contract. Useful for catching donor awards whose winners are regional systems integrators and payment vendors.

source_name: Open Data Kosovo — e-Prokurimi municipal procurement app and API (open-source)
why_relevant: ODK built an early municipal-procurement dataset and an open-source API (github.com/opendatakosovo/e-prokurimi-api) covering procurement plans, tender dossiers and signed contract PDFs at municipal level, plus red-flag methodology. Valuable for the pre-2020 historical layer that the current OCDS feed and Red Flags do not cover, and its code documents field semantics.

source_name: CEFTA Transparency Pack — Public Procurement (Kosovo entry)
why_relevant: Regional trade-portal summary of Kosovo's procurement regime with links to the authoritative portals and legal basis; a compact, stable orientation source for confirming which body publishes what, useful when validating the source map.

source_name: Global Public Procurement Database (GPPD) — Kosovo (XK) country profile
why_relevant: World Bank-hosted normalised procurement statistics by country; provides benchmark spend aggregates and category breakdowns that can sanity-check any bottom-up sizing built from Kosovo award notices.

source_name: Serbian Government Office for Kosovo and Metohija (Kancelarija za KiM) — javne nabavke section
source_subtype: foreign-government procurement notices affecting the territory
why_relevant: A parallel, Serbia-funded public spending channel touching Kosovo-Serb-majority municipalities and parallel institutions, published under Serbian procurement rules in Serbian. Relevant because banking/payment arrangements in the north (e.g. cash handling, account services for Serbia-funded institutions) do not appear in Kosovo's e-Prokurimi at all.

source_name: EBRD Project Finder / Project Summary Documents (Kosovo)
why_relevant: EBRD is the largest institutional investor in Kosovo (cumulative ~EUR 827m across ~133 projects). Project Summary Documents name the exact bank counterparty (NLB Banka Prishtina, ProCredit Bank Kosovo, Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo, Banka per Biznes, TEB), instrument, ticket size, use of proceeds (SME, green, digitalisation) and signing status - counterparty-level disclosure not available from domestic sources.

source_name: EBRD Newsroom - Kosovo financial-institution transactions
why_relevant: Press releases are the fastest signal of a signed credit line and usually state the partner bank, amount, EU co-funding vehicle (SME Go Green, SME Reboot, GEFF WB) and any digitalisation/technical-assistance component. Verified 2024-2025 items exist for NLB Banka Prishtina (EUR 20m incl. digital transformation), ProCredit Bank Kosovo (EUR 13m) and Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo (EUR 5m).

source_name: EBRD Client e-Procurement Portal (ECEPP) + EBRD procurement notices
why_relevant: Where EBRD-financed public-sector procurement (including IT/payment-systems and consultancy for financial-sector clients) is tendered and awarded. Award notices reveal which vendors are being selected for Kosovo financial infrastructure work - directly competitive intelligence for a payments vendor.

source_name: World Bank Documents & Reports - Kosovo financial sector operations
why_relevant: Holds the full document chain (PAD, ISR, PID, ICR, procurement plans) for Kosovo Financial Sector Strengthening Project (P165147) and Kosovo Financial Sector Development (P507881, ~USD 52m, aimed at deposit insurance capacity, underserved-firm finance and 'catalysing faster payments'). PADs contain the most detailed public description of Kosovo's instant-payments/RTGS modernisation agenda and its budget lines.

source_name: World Bank Projects & Operations - Kosovo portfolio
why_relevant: Canonical index of active/closed Kosovo operations with project ids, commitment amounts, approval and closing dates, and implementing agency (CBK, Ministry of Finance). Best entry point to snowball into all downstream documents and procurement plans.

source_name: IFC Disclosure Portal / Project Information & Data Portal
why_relevant: IFC investments and advisory projects in Kosovo banks are disclosed here (Summary of Investment Information, advisory project summaries). IFC's Kosovo advisory work with the Central Bank of Kosovo on digital financial services, the payment-services law and open banking is the single most payments-relevant donor programme in the country.

source_name: IFC Pressroom - Albanian-language Kosovo releases
why_relevant: Confirms IFC publishes Kosovo announcements in Albanian. The sq versions carry the local institutional terminology ('sherbimet financiare digjitale', 'Banka Qendrore e Republikes se Kosoves', 'ligji per sherbimet e pagesave') needed to seed local-language monitoring of the same programmes in domestic media.
